sections.html:
Russellville is the county seat and largest city of Pope County, on the southern edge of the Ozark Mountains and north of the Arkansas River. It sits at an elevation of 367 feet, and the city covers about 28 square miles.

Pope County stretches across about 831 square miles. The Arkansas River Valley lies in the south, with farmland and towns, while the Ozarks, including part of the Boston Mountains, cover nearly two-thirds of the county to the north. About 40% of the county is in the Ozark National Forest, and the Holla Bend National Wildlife Refuge manages about 7,055 acres.

The other incorporated places in the county are Atkins, Dover, London and Pottsville. The county is dry, meaning alcohol sales are prohibited In 2018 Pope County was one of four counties designated for casino licenses under Amendment 100, and in November 2024 Issue 2 removed it from that amendment.

sections.h2: How did Russellville become the county seat?
sections.html:
Russellville won the Pope County seat in a March 19, 1887 election, beating Atkins by 128 votes out of 2,670 cast. Dover had been the seat since 1841.

The first house was a hand-hewn log house built in 1834 by J. C. Holledger and bought in 1835 by Dr. Thomas Russell, for whom the town was named around 1842. The area was once called Chactas Prairie or Cactus Flats. Incorporation came on June 7, 1870, and railroad construction in the early 1870s took the town from about 240 residents in 1870 to about 800 by 1876.

A fire on January 16, 1906 destroyed nearly half of the downtown business district, including 23 buildings. Interstate 40 construction began in 1956 and spurred growth, and a dam completed in 1965 created Lake Dardanelle.

Russellville's economy rests on manufacturing, a nuclear plant, a university and a lake. About 50 manufacturing plants employ more than 8,300 people, and more than ten divisions of Fortune 500 companies have facilities in the city.

  • Tyson Foods is a notable employer.
  • Arkansas Nuclear One, the state's only nuclear power plant, was built just outside the city in the 1970s.
  • Products made locally include frozen dinners, railroad crossties, parking meters, aluminum foil, graphite electrodes and aircraft and automotive parts.
  • Coal mining was once a major industry, but no coal is mined today.
  • Lake Dardanelle supports tourism, fishing tournaments and state park activity.

Owners who take a job at one of these employers, or leave one, often need to sell on a short timeline, and an as-is sale is one way to meet it.

sections.h2: What do the weather and the lake mean for a Russellville house?
sections.html:
Russellville is hot in summer and mild in winter, and rainfall peaks in spring. At the Russellville Municipal Airport, the 1991 to 2020 normals show an average January daily high of 50.3 degrees and a July daily high of 92.5 degrees. Annual precipitation averages 46.41 inches on about 113.7 days, and April (4.83 inches) and May (4.67 inches) are the wettest months.

The record high is 115 degrees in August, and the record low is minus 15 degrees.

  • A July average near 92 degrees means the cooling system is among the first things a buyer asks about.
  • Spring rain concentrates the roof, gutter and drainage questions into April and May.
  • A house near the river or lake should be checked against FEMA flood maps for that address.

The McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System passes the area, and Lake Dardanelle is a reservoir created by the 1965 dam, so lakefront and riverfront values depend on the specific lot.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Russellville?
sections.html:
The Russellville Public School District was formed in 1870, and Arkansas Tech University, which began in 1910 as the Second District Agricultural School, sits in the city. It became Arkansas Polytechnic College in 1925 and took its current name in 1976.

Interstate 40 is the main road, and rail service linking Fort Smith and Little Rock has run since the 1870s. Little Rock National is the major commercial airport, and Russellville Municipal Airport is a local field.

During the 2024 solar eclipse, the city had 4 minutes 11 seconds of totality and hosted about 60,000 visitors.

sections.h2: How does Russellville code enforcement work?
sections.html:
Russellville code enforcement handles property maintenance, vegetation, building violations, zoning violations and sign violations. A neighbor can report a concern by phone, in person or through the online Code Enforcement Requests portal, and an officer then inspects.

  • If no violation is found, the case closes.
  • If one is confirmed, a Notice of Violation is mailed to the owner and to the violation address when it differs.
  • The owner can fix the problem or submit a plan of repair to request more time.
  • If the violation remains, the city may issue civil penalties or pursue abatement.

The code enforcement office is at 107 North El Paso Avenue, phone 479-967-2633, and City Hall is at 203 S. Commerce Avenue, phone 479-968-2098. If you inherit a house and a notice arrives, respond quickly with a plan of repair, or sell the property as-is to a buyer who will take on the work.

sections.h2: How do Pope County taxes and a Russellville closing work?
sections.html:
The Pope County Tax Collector is on the second floor of the courthouse at 100 West Main Street in Russellville. Tax books open March 1 and close October 15, and penalties are added after that date. If October 15 falls on a weekend or a post office holiday, taxes are due the next business day.

The collector explains that real estate tax bills go to the owner of record on January 1 of the previous year, because taxes are paid one year in arrears. If the property sells during the year, the closing documents say whether buyer or seller is responsible for the bill. When a lender escrows taxes, the statement goes to the lender only on written request.

If real estate taxes go unpaid for two consecutive years, the land is certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, stays at the state level for two years and is then sold at auction. The Pope County Assessor, in the same courthouse at 479-968-7418, values real property at current market value based on comparable sales.

At recording, Arkansas charges a $3.30 per $1,000 transfer tax paid by a stamp. The state does not require every seller to disclose all known defects, and the Seller Property Disclosure form is encouraged but optional.

faqs.q: How many people live in Russellville?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 28,940 people, and the 2025 estimate is 29,521. Pope County had 63,381 residents in 2020.

faqs.q: When are Pope County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The tax books open March 1 and close October 15, and penalties are added afterward. If the date falls on a weekend or post office holiday, payment is due the next business day.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax when a Russellville house sells?
faqs.a: The closing documents decide. Pope County's collector says tax bills go to the owner of record on January 1 of the previous year because taxes are paid one year in arrears.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore a Russellville code violation notice?
faqs.a: The city may issue civil penalties or pursue abatement after re-inspection. You can request more time by submitting a plan of repair to the officer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Russellville house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but start early. After two consecutive unpaid years, land can be certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, so resolving the balance before that point gives you more options.
